items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: But anyhow Clowns Todd was on piano, Chiff and me was on trumpets, and this Ben man, I can't think of his name.

ctx.x: They call him Ben or something like that?

Yeah, Ben. His name must have been Benjamin but they called him Ben. But anyhow Clowns Todd was on piano, Chiff and me was on trumpets, and this Ben man, I can't think of his name. To tell you the truth I think the Moosef was from New Orleans but I just can't think of him now. But the Moosef was right out of New Orleans.
Well how did Clowns Todd play? What kind of piano?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Him and that old tram boy called Paul Ben, Kaza, and his brother.

ctx.x: He was a straight reader, but he played out there with P. Ron. And Kemba was a straight reader, but he could... He could...

But all them boys was out there in the field like me, all them got off, I ain't kidding, every one of them. Every one of them. Now this Louis Demand, he didn't get off, but he always had good music. What about a guy like Kaza? Kaza played with Sackton. Clarinet and Sackton. Clarinet and Sackton, yeah, he played good, but I never did wake with Kaza. Was he a get off man? Yeah, he played pretty good. He used to play with that tall face of Teach. Teach right here, you know him. What a guy's name in there. He was the…
This guy was a trumpet player, Tom.
